entry.title: Pointe de la Torche
entry.summary: A wide sandy beach beside the Pointe de la Torche in south Finistere, one of the best-known surf spots in Brittany. The waves are often big, and the spot is open all year to experienced surfers.

entry.title: Plage de la Palue
entry.summary: A wild sandy beach on the west coast of the Crozon peninsula in Brittany, popular with surfers for its Atlantic waves. A car park on the dune top gives a short walk to the sand.

entry.title: Plage de Tahiti
entry.summary: The northern end of the long Pampelonne bay near Ramatuelle on the French Riviera, with fine sand and a line of beach restaurants. Public access to the beach is free.

entry.title: Plage de Piemanson
entry.summary: A long, wild sandy beach on the Camargue coast near the mouth of the Rhone, with dunes and few buildings. It is known for kitesurfing and for its long-standing wild camping season.

entry.title: Pakostane Beach
entry.summary: A pine-shaded bay on the coast between Zadar and Sibenik, with a mix of sand, shingle and rocky terraces. Pine trees run down almost to the shore.

entry.title: Nin Beach
entry.summary: Queen Beach (Kraljicina plaza) is a sandy beach of more than 2 km on the Nin lagoon near Zadar. The water stays shallow for up to about 500 m from the shore, which suits small children. The lagoon bed is sand and mud and shifts with the weather.

entry.title: Zavala Beach
entry.summary: A pebble and gravel beach in the village of Zavala on the quiet south coast of Hvar. The village is reached from Pitve through a tunnel, with a signposted car park near the beach.

entry.title: Kupari Beach
entry.summary: A pebble beach in Zupa dubrovacka, about 10 km south of Dubrovnik, beside the shell of a military holiday resort built for Yugoslav army officers. The hotels have been abandoned since the 1991 siege of Dubrovnik, and redevelopment work began on the site in 2025.

entry.title: Stara Baska Beach
entry.summary: A long bay at the southern tip of Krk with fine gravel and pebbles and clear water, framed by bare limestone hills. One road runs through the village.

entry.title: Playa de Calblanque
entry.summary: A string of sandy coves inside Calblanque Regional Park on the Murcia coast, with dunes and low hills and no buildings behind the beach. Car access is restricted in summer to protect the park.

entry.title: Cala Torta
entry.summary: A wide, undeveloped sand beach on the north-east coast of Mallorca near Arta, with golden sand and clear water. The final approach is a walk from an unpaved parking area.

entry.title: Playa de Los Lances
entry.summary: A long, open sandy beach on the Strait of Gibraltar just north-west of Tarifa, known for kitesurfing and windsurfing. Africa is visible across the water on clear days.

entry.title: Praia da Salema
entry.summary: A Blue Flag beach beside the fishing village of Salema on the western Algarve, with golden sand between low cliffs and a line of beachfront restaurants.

entry.title: Praia da Ingrina
entry.summary: A small sandy cove on the western Algarve near Raposeira, sheltered by rocks. A seafood restaurant sits by the sand with views over the bay.

entry.title: Praia do Zavial
entry.summary: A broad sandy bay on the western Algarve, backed by low cliffs and a beachfront restaurant. The Atlantic water is cooler than on the central Algarve and waves can be strong.

entry.title: Calamosche Beach
entry.summary: A small sandy cove between rocky headlands inside the Vendicari nature reserve on the south-east coast of Sicily. The beach is reached on foot from the car park and has no shade.

entry.title: Punta Prosciutto
entry.summary: A long sandy beach on the Ionian coast of Salento, backed by dunes and part of a protected area within the Porto Cesareo marine reserve. It mixes free sand with paid lido areas.

entry.title: Fiascherino Beach
entry.summary: A small cove on the Gulf of La Spezia between Lerici and Tellaro. Two beaches sit on either side of a rocky promontory, with steps leading down to the water.

entry.title: Sa Colonia Beach
entry.summary: A sandy beach at Chia on the south coast of Sardinia, with a coastal lagoon behind it where pink flamingos sometimes feed. The area has kiosks and small services but no large beach clubs.

entry.title: Kolona Beach
entry.summary: A narrow strip of fine sand joining the main island of Kythnos to the islet of Agios Loukas, with water on both sides. It is widely described as the most famous beach on the island.

entry.title: Porto Timoni
entry.summary: Two back-to-back coves on the north-west coast of Corfu, separated by a narrow strip of land. The only way in is on foot from the village of Afionas along a rocky path.

entry.title: Kalamitsi Beach
entry.summary: A string of pebble coves on the west coast of Lefkada below the village of Kalamitsi, with clear water under steep cliffs. Kavalikefta, Megali Petra and Avali lie close together along the same rough road.

entry.title: Agios Sostis Beach
entry.summary: A quiet sandy beach on the north coast of Mykonos, far from the busy clubs of the south. The beach is undeveloped, with no organised sunbeds and a single taverna nearby.

entry.title: Super Paradise Beach
entry.summary: A sandy cove on the south coast of Mykonos, known for its beach clubs and lively atmosphere. The beach sits below a steep access road, with clear water and a mix of paid and open sand.

entry.title: Kavourotrypes Beach
entry.summary: A string of small coves on the east coast of Sithonia, also known as Orange Beach. White rocks frame clear turquoise water, with small patches of sand between the outcrops.

entry.title: Praia do Vale do Lobo
entry.summary: A wide sandy beach below the ochre cliffs of the Vale do Lobo resort on the central Algarve. The Praca area above the beach holds restaurants and bars, and a Blue Flag has been reported.

entry.title: Marina Grande Beach
entry.summary: A small public beach of volcanic sand and rocks beside the old fishing harbour of Marina Grande in Sorrento, with colourful houses and restaurants around it.

entry.title: Alimini Beach
entry.summary: A stretch of fine sand and clear, gently sloping water on the Salento coast near Otranto, backed by pine woods and dunes. Free stretches sit between beach bars and resort beaches.

entry.title: Agios Gordios Beach
entry.summary: A Blue Flag beach of about 1 km on the west coast of Corfu, backed by steep green cliffs and a rock offshore. The south end is sandy and the north end gets pebblier.

entry.title: Tamariu Beach
entry.summary: A small golden-sand bay of roughly 180 m in the village of Tamariu, sheltered by pine-covered headlands on the Costa Brava. Fishing boats sit on the sand and a row of cafes and restaurants lines the seafront.
